title: Blackstone-backed AirTrunk to invest $1 billion in Japan data centre campus
source_used: Reuters brief as carried by AOL; text from WORKDIR/fulltext/C09-16.txt
key_facts: Blackstone-backed AirTrunk said on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026 it is investing an additional $1 billion in its 300-plus-megawatt data center campus in Inzai, Japan.
The money is for liquid-cooling technology so the campus can run AI workloads.
It secured a $1 billion green loan led by Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp, MUFG Bank and United Overseas Bank, among others.
The campus, TOK1, is likely the first in Japan with large-scale AI workloads, CEO Robin Khuda says.
Khuda says AI infrastructure will get harder in the US and is already hard in Europe, making Asia a beneficiary.
quote_evidence: TOKYO, Oct 7 (Reuters) - Blackstone-backed AirTrunk said on Wednesday it was investing an additional $1 billion in its 300-plus-megawatt hyperscale data centre campus in the eastern Japanese city of Inzai to enable AI workloads.
Investment is for liquid-cooling technology deployment to enable AI workload
why_it_matters_hint: An Asian data center builder is adding AI cooling capacity and says siting is getting harder in the US and Europe.
notes: Short Reuters bullet brief carried by AOL; original Reuters link not seen.
